_fixture_note: Adversarial fixture, not a regression fixture. Purpose: every other fixture here has every floor corner at y=0.0 and an origin-anchored polygon — a bug that silently depends on y being exactly 0, or on the polygon starting at (0,0), would pass all of them and still be wrong. Mark found exactly this class of bug on a real device (2026-09-02): the iOS exporter passed a floor's local-frame corners straight through without applying surface.transform, and every existing fixture (client and server) happened to already look like valid world-space data, so nothing caught it. This floor sits at y=-2.5 (a non-zero height) and is translated well away from the origin (x in [10.0, 13.5], z in [-5.0, -2.2]) — same 3.5m x 2.8m rectangle as roomplan_captured_room_single_room.json's shape, translated, so the expected area (9.8 m2) and perimeter (12.6 m) are still hand-verifiable.
